axes: Unity metres. Authored in Unity axes; Blender = (-x, -z, y); FBX export -Z forward, Y up, bake_space_transform (the fish settings). Each FBX object is at the origin with an identity transform: place each at the Unity origin.

encoding.uv0: UVMap: wood in metres, grain along u (long axis; posts and lathes grain up); _Tri objects: world xz
encoding.uv1: Layer: (palette slot, texture layer) on every corner; no uv1.z in the FBX (the mapping comes from the material: _Tri -> M_Toon_Tri, else M_Toon_Base)
encoding.colour: Col: 0.5 x ao (half-scale grey, _JitterEncoded 1); ao = per-vertex BVH ray-cast bake in Blender (40 rays, 1 m, terrain occluder, back faces ignored) above a per-part floor (wood 0.45, rock 0.62)

items_note: Per FBX, items lists every placed piece: position and footprint are the world AABB (Unity axes, yaw included) of its geometry; sphere items (rocks, boulders) give the sphere centre and radius (the mesh is inside it) plus bounds_min/max. Place rock and boulder colliders from these numbers; never re-draw the rocks in C# (Python random.Random is not Pcg32).
notes: uv1.z (mapping) is not in the FBX: RenderValidators.ToonMeshMappingMatchesMaterial expects uv1.z == 1 on M_Toon_Tri, so the builder writes uv1.z = 1 into the _Tri mesh copies or the validator exempts them.

Layout deviations: west-front T-head bollard at (-3.9, -5.4) to clear the lamp at (-4.8, -5.3); deck stringers at x +-1.38 (under the plank ends, resting on the posts); ladder grab rails rise to y 2.35 (inside the rail boxes); post foot flares reach 2 cm below TerrainY; the hut roof, ridge roll and stove pipe exceed the 4 x 3 x 3 m box (see the Hut item bounds); lamps top out at y 4.53.

Breakwater boulders overhang the x 28..32 collider box by up to ~1.9 m at the waterline and the rubble base reaches x ~25 / ~35 (top y ~ -0.48): add per-boulder sphere colliders from the items or widen the box at water level, or swimmers pass into rock.

pass2.summary: Detail pass: dunes, paths, stone wall, headlands, river mouth, coast road; bait shop, net shed, smokehouse, harbour office; yard props and clutter; plants and shoreline; lighthouse, islands, stacks, far boats; the crew tugboat (R76).

groups.core: always drawn; every pass-2 collider belongs to a core model
groups.detail: no colliders; hide on the Low preset

notes: Placement: every pass-2 FBX object is at the origin with an identity transform. World models: place at the Unity origin. Local models (local_space true: the tug, its collision mesh, the ice chest, the Anim_* pieces): instantiate once per placement at position with yaw_deg about +y. Ice chest placements are in the CrewBoat local frame (parent them to the placed tug).

Materials: "_Tri" -> M_Toon_Tri (the HarbourModelPostprocessor uv1.z fix applies), others M_Toon_Base, Harbour_Core_River -> the water material (no palette slot fits water; it also holds the tide-pool discs). Col models: MeshCollider only, no renderer.
Low preset: hide every group "detail" model. No detail model carries a collider, so Low changes nothing in gameplay.

Colliders: box items -> BoxCollider from bounds_min/max (Structure layer like the phase-1 props, except the stone wall and gate pillars: Shore). Walkable land: Harbour_Dunes_Col (MeshCollider, Shore layer, inside the walls only). The tug: Harbour_Core_CrewBoat_Col (MeshCollider on the placed tug; walkable decks, deckhouse interior, upper deck, wheelhouse). Tug ladders: LadderVolume boxes from Harbour_Core_CrewBoat.ladders (local frame). Ice chests: a BoxCollider each (size in the placement).

Code trees: the 16 HarbourPierBuilder trees still stand on the plateau (y 1.2): the dunes are flattened within ~1.3 m of each trunk and ramp up from 4.6 m, so no tree floats or sinks. Pass-2 buildings and props keep >= 2.5 m from each trunk (positions ported from Pcg32). Their visuals are the four local Harbour_Core_CodeTree_* models (round 0): one placement per Tree_NN, parented under it so its localScale (the Pcg32 height) scales the tree and the trunk and canopy colliders stay as they were.
Backdrop (hills, cliffs, forest, islands, road, backdrop, river): no colliders; outside the walls; invisible to the bake.
Beach foam: the code beach/water already draws the foam line and wet edge at the coast; no extra foam mesh was added.

The in-water solid objects are the tug (hull box or its MeshCollider) and the gangway; everything else in the water is visual only (floats, seaweed, gull on a buoy, river and pool water). See verification for their clearance from the stand circles and cast lanes.

No add-on output and no downloaded asset is exported (assets_used stays empty): trees (layered branch clumps), rock masses, dunes and hills are procedural in fg_harbour.py, so a rebuild from an empty file with --factory-startup needs no add-on and stays deterministic.

The .blend carries preview-only toon materials (FG_Preview_Toon*, palette from ArtPalette.asset Summer) and a built-in sky for the build-log renders; export_fbx strips every material, so none reaches the FBX.
